title: 3D Vision & NeRF
motto: 3D vision comes in two flavours. Point clouds are the sensor's raw output. NeRFs are the learned volumetric field. Both answer "what is where in space."

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: 3D vision comes in two flavours. Point clouds are the sensor's raw output. NeRFs are the learned volumetric field. Both answer "what is where in space."

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: A camera produces a 2D image. A LIDAR produces a set of 3D points with no ordering. A structure-from-motion pipeline produces a sparse cloud of 3D keypoints. A NeRF reconstructs an entire 3D scene from a handful of posed images. All of these are "vision" but none of them look like the dense tensor a CNN wants.

3D vision matters because almost every high-value robot task runs in 3D: grasping, obstacle avoidance, navigation, AR occlusion, 3D content capture. A vision engineer who only understands 2D images is locked out of the fastest-growing slice of the field (AR/VR content, robotics, autonomous driving stacks, NeRF-based 3D reconstruction for real-estate or construction).

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: NeRF represents a scene as a neural radiance field — query density and color along rays.
